routes.label: Insert 3-2 and telescope differences of squares.

question: Which of the following is equivalent to \[ \begin{aligned} &(2+3)(2^2+3^2)\\ &\quad\cdot(2^4+3^4)(2^8+3^8)\\ &\quad\cdot(2^{16}+3^{16})(2^{32}+3^{32})\\ &\quad\cdot(2^{64}+3^{64})? \end{aligned} \]
solution:
The exponents double at every step, which matches repeated use of \((u-v)(u+v)=u^2-v^2\). Insert the harmless factor \(3-2=1\) at the start.

The first cancellations are
\[
(3-2)(3+2)=3^2-2^2,
\]
\[
(3^2-2^2)(3^2+2^2)=3^4-2^4.
\]
Each next sum turns the current difference into a new difference with doubled exponents. After the last factor \(3^{64}+2^{64}\), the product is
\[
\boxed{3^{128}-2^{128}},
\]
choice C. A sequence of doubling exponents is a clue to build a chain of differences of squares.
